_meta.title: Humanoid Robots: A Living Atlas
_meta.note: Editorial / educational comparison. Specs are sourced from official company pages where available and labeled by confidence. Where a value is not publicly disclosed it is set to null with confidence 'unknown'. Visual proxies render as Three.js primitives unless an accurate GLB has been added and verifiedModel is set true.

confidence_legend.official: Direct from the company's own product / spec page or a primary release.
confidence_legend.reported: Stated by the company in a press appearance or interview, but not on an official spec page.
confidence_legend.estimated: A range or reasonable extrapolation from public material; not the company's own number.
confidence_legend.unknown: Not publicly confirmed. Avoid reading too much into the procedural model proxy.

aiSystem.value: Vision-language model partnership with OpenAI for end-to-end demos

robots.summary: Figure's first-generation humanoid. The platform that demonstrated dialogue-driven manipulation in their March 2024 OpenAI partnership demo, then was rapidly superseded by Figure 02.
differentiators: End-to-end vision-language driven manipulation demo with OpenAI
Compact glossy-black faceplate visual identity
First Figure platform to ship press demos

aiSystem.value: Helix vision-language-action model (Figure-developed, replacing the OpenAI partnership)

robots.summary: Figure 02 added third-generation hands, integrated cameras, and a 3x compute upgrade. Marks Figure's pivot from research-demo platform to pilot-deployment platform.
differentiators: In-house Helix VLA replaces the OpenAI partnership
Larger battery and 3x compute over Figure 01
Third-generation hands with improved manipulation envelope

changesFromPrevious.text: Switched from the OpenAI partnership to Figure's own Helix VLA model.
Third-generation hands with improved dexterity and force range.
Battery, integrated cameras, and 3x onboard compute relative to Figure 01.
Shifted from research demo to industrial pilot positioning.

robots.summary: Figure's current featured platform. The official Figure page positions Figure 03 as a general-purpose humanoid leaning into home environments, but most spec disclosure is still pending.
differentiators: Home-environment framing in the official product page
Continues the smooth glossy-black face visual identity
Positioned as Figure's current commercial showcase

changesFromPrevious.text: Shifts emphasis from industrial pilots toward home environments.
Continues Helix VLA, with form-factor refinements over Figure 02.

aiSystem.value: Stated reuse of Tesla Autopilot vision stack

robots.summary: The first publicly walking Optimus prototype, shown at Tesla AI Day 2022. Built largely from off-the-shelf parts to demonstrate the program existed.
differentiators: First public Optimus on stage
Off-the-shelf actuators, used as proof of life rather than a product
Public framing tied to Tesla's broader AI / Autopilot stack

aiSystem.value: Shared neural-network stack with Tesla Autopilot

robots.summary: First in-house Tesla-built Optimus generation. Replaced the off-the-shelf hardware of the prototype with Tesla-designed actuators and a custom hand.
differentiators: First fully Tesla-designed Optimus body
Custom 11-DoF hand framing in public demos
Walked across stage at Tesla events

changesFromPrevious.text: Replaced off-the-shelf actuators with Tesla in-house designs.
Introduced an 11-DoF custom hand featured in demos.

status.value: Public demos and Tesla factory pilots

weight.value: ~10 kg lighter than Gen 1 (per Tesla demo video)

speed.value: ~30% faster walking than Gen 1 (per Tesla demo)

robots.summary: Tesla's December 2023 reveal of a noticeably lighter, faster, more refined Optimus. The first version that read as a product silhouette rather than an engineering prototype.
differentiators: Reportedly ~10 kg lighter and ~30% faster walking than Gen 1
Refined silhouette closer to a finished product
Demonstrated finer manipulation tasks in Tesla videos

changesFromPrevious.text: Walking speed reportedly ~30% higher than Gen 1.
~10 kg lighter, more refined silhouette.
Smoother demonstrated manipulation tasks in Tesla video reveals.

robots.summary: Tesla has publicly framed a third-generation Optimus as the production-targeted version. Specifications remain largely unverified in public material; treat as forward-looking.
differentiators: Positioned as the first production-targeted Optimus
Public framing tied to Tesla AI day announcements
Specific specs largely unverified

changesFromPrevious.text: Framed as the first production-targeted Optimus rather than an internal prototype.

robots.summary: The original parkour-running, gymnastics-doing Atlas. The hydraulic platform that made Boston Dynamics a household name and was retired in April 2024 in favor of an electric successor.
differentiators: Hydraulic actuation, distinctive sound and athleticism
Showcased dynamic parkour and gymnastic motion
Retired April 2024 in favor of Electric Atlas

robots.summary: The all-electric successor to the hydraulic Atlas. Marked Boston Dynamics's pivot from research showcase to commercial industrial humanoid, with Hyundai as the launch deployment partner.
differentiators: All-electric replacement for the hydraulic platform
Commercial / industrial framing rather than research showcase
Hyundai pilot deployment partnership

changesFromPrevious.text: Switched from hydraulic to all-electric actuation.
Pivoted from research platform to commercial / industrial use.
New range of motion exceeds typical human-joint limits in early demos.

robots.summary: Agility's first commercially available Digit. Notable for its bird-like reverse-bent legs and lack of a head; a deliberately functional warehouse design.
differentiators: Distinctive ostrich-style reverse-bent legs
Headless sensor-bar silhouette
Material-handling positioning from day one

targetEnvironment.value: Warehouse logistics, tote and case handling

aiSystem.value: Agility Arc cloud platform for fleet operation

robots.summary: Current-generation Digit. Adds a perception head, refined hands, and Agility's Arc cloud platform for managing fleets of robots in real warehouses.
differentiators: Adds a perception head with cameras
Arc cloud fleet management platform
Active commercial deployments at warehouse customers

changesFromPrevious.text: Refined hands and end effectors for tote / case handling.
Arc cloud fleet platform brings central monitoring and OTA updates.
From R&D pilots to ongoing commercial warehouse deployments.

robots.summary: Apollo is Apptronik's modular general-purpose humanoid, framed for industrial and commercial work first. Builds on Apptronik's NASA Valkyrie lineage; designed around a hot-swappable battery.
differentiators: Hot-swappable battery for continuous operation
Status-light chest module for human-robot interaction
Modular industrial design lineage from NASA Valkyrie

robots.summary: 1X's first commercially deployed humanoid. Wheeled base instead of legs; soft tendon-driven upper body. A practical R&D platform that paved the way for NEO.
differentiators: Wheeled base instead of bipedal walking
Tendon-driven upper body for safer human contact
First 1X platform in active deployments

robots.summary: NEO is 1X's bipedal home humanoid. Soft, fabric-covered, deliberately quiet, designed to operate in domestic spaces. Early access ships with explicit teleoperation and autonomy caveats.
differentiators: Bipedal soft-bodied home humanoid
Fabric / soft-suit exterior to soften human-contact concerns
Early-access program with explicit teleoperation disclosure

changesFromPrevious.text: Bipedal walking instead of wheeled base.
Soft-suit exterior and lighter weight for home environments.
Targets home users via early-access rather than commercial security pilots.

robots.summary: H1 was Unitree's first general-purpose humanoid. Notable for combining respectable specs with research-developer pricing far below Western competitors.
differentiators: Affordable research-grade humanoid pricing
Strong sprint speed for a research platform
Open SDK for developers

robots.summary: H1-2 is the second iteration of Unitree's H1 platform with refined hardware. Most published spec deltas vs the original H1 are still pending in publicly cited material.
differentiators: Iterated hardware refinements over H1
Same affordability and SDK posture
Continues athletic-research positioning

changesFromPrevious.text: Hardware refinements over H1; specific deltas largely undisclosed in cited material.

robots.summary: G1 is Unitree's smaller, more affordable general-purpose humanoid. Compact athletic design at a price point that opened humanoid hardware to many more research labs.
differentiators: Smaller, more affordable humanoid platform
Up to 43 DoF in extended configuration
Made humanoid R&D accessible at significantly lower cost

robots.summary: Fourier's first general-purpose humanoid, leveraging the company's rehabilitation-robotics lineage. Strong reported payload for its weight class; details confirmed mostly in press material.
differentiators: Strong reported payload-to-weight ratio
Rehabilitation-robotics design lineage
Research and industrial trial positioning

aiSystem.value: Fourier in-house controllers, open APIs for integration

robots.summary: GR-2 is Fourier's documented second-generation humanoid. The official GR-2 documentation portal exposes spec details that put the platform credibly in the research / industrial-trial bracket.
differentiators: Public documentation portal with spec disclosure
53 DoF for fine manipulation tasks
Integration APIs for research labs and manufacturing pilots

changesFromPrevious.text: Higher overall DoF count and refined hands relative to GR-1.
Public APIs and documentation expose more integration surface.

aiSystem.value: UBTECH service-robot stack with face/voice interaction

robots.summary: UBTECH's smart-home / service-robot humanoid. Distinctive screen face and service-bot proportions, used for retail showcases and home demonstrations rather than industrial labor.
differentiators: Screen-face for human-robot interaction
Strongly service-oriented platform
41 active DoF in a small frame

targetEnvironment.value: Work tasks across retail, logistics, manufacturing

degreesOfFreedom.value: Hands feature 20+ DoF each, per Sanctuary

robots.summary: Sanctuary's first publicly unveiled general-purpose humanoid, framed as the body for the company's Carbon AI software. Emphasizes dexterous human-equivalent hands and work-task generality.
differentiators: Marketed dexterous hands with 20+ DoF each
Carbon AI software stack as the headline differentiator
Described as 6th-generation Sanctuary technology
